title: Whose is this? Kenen …?
summary: Ask whose one thing is using the basic noun and tämä on.
objectives: Ask whose one thing is using the basic noun and tämä on.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Ask about an unspecified owner
paragraphs: Kenen means “whose”, an owner-question form of kuka (“who”). The owner is unspecified, so add no personal possessive suffix.
Use Kenen + basic noun + tämä on?: Kenen pallo tämä on? (“Whose ball is this?”). Kenen tämä pallo on? is also ordinary word order.
Kenen does not establish how many people own the thing or things. Explicit questions about several owners are outside this pattern. Typed and token tasks accept both taught word orders.
keyPoints: no personal suffix on the question noun

steps: Begin with Kenen (“whose”) to ask about an unspecified owner.
Use pallo (“ball”) without a personal possessive suffix.
Use tämä on for the one thing being identified.
Begin with Kenen (“whose”) to ask about an unspecified owner.
Use auto (“car”) without a personal possessive suffix.
Use tämä on for the one thing being identified.

commonMistakes: Do not add a personal suffix to the question noun.
The number of things does not determine the number of owners.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Write “Whose apple is this?” in Finnish. Begin with Kenen. Use omena (“apple”), tämä on (“this is”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed basic noun and tämä on.

parts.formation: Kenen is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”). Several things do not by themselves change kenen.
Keep the basic singular noun without a personal suffix.
Use on with singular tämä; ask whose with kenen.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Remove the personal ending from talosi (“your house”) to complete “Whose house is this?”: Kenen ___ tämä on? The owner is unknown. Write only the basic noun.
practiceExercises.explanation: Talosi is talo + -si (“your”). Kenen leaves the owner unknown: remove -si and use basic talo.

parts.role: thing whose owner is asked about
parts.formation: Talosi is talo + -si (“your”). Remove -si because kenen leaves the owner unknown; use basic singular talo.

answerDiagnostics.category: Whose questions with kenen: form or meaning confused
answerDiagnostics.explanation: A personal possessive ending names an owner. Kenen asks who the unknown owner is: remove -si from talosi and use basic talo.
